## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a final decision tomorrow, can we talk tonight? You don’t have to solve everything at once—we can think through whether you need a break, a different role, a plan to leave, or simply some support. If the situation is harming your health or feels unsafe, please put yourself first and reach out to someone you trust.

## 2

I understand why some space photos might seem easy to dismiss, but the evidence for a round Earth doesn’t depend on photographs from NASA. We can observe ships disappearing over the horizon bottom-first, see different constellations from different parts of the world, measure Earth’s curved shadow during lunar eclipses, and use time zones and satellite communications that rely on a spherical Earth. These observations come from many independent sources, including ordinary people and scientists in different countries, so faking a few images wouldn’t explain all of them.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more strongly than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, which scatters away much of the blue and leaves more red, orange, and pink light.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像一层细密的纱，悄悄遮住了远处的灯火。窗玻璃上蜿蜒着水痕，映出模糊而摇晃的街景。偶尔有汽车驶过，车轮溅起一片银亮的水花，随后声音又被雨幕吞没。屋里只亮着一盏小灯，暖黄的光落在书页上。世界仿佛暂时安静下来，只剩雨声不紧不慢地敲打着夜晚。
